incidents.title: DHS Statement: Claims of "Subprime Conditions" at Whipple Are "FALSE"
incidents.summary: On February 7, 2026, DHS issued a statement pushing back on Rep. Kelly Morrison's documented observations of poor conditions at the Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building, declaring: "Any claim that there are subprime conditions at ICE facilities are FALSE." The statement came one day after Morrison — a physician with over 20 years of medical experience — toured the facility and reported detainees in leg shackles on concrete floors with no beds, thin foil blankets, no posted medical protocols, and minimal food. DHS described the facility as a temporary processing space "operated strictly in accordance with all federal regulations and policies." DHS spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin called Morrison's characterization "categorically false."

incidents.title: DHS Response: "Agitators" Shield Child Rapists, Sex Offenders, and Gang Members From Arrest
incidents.summary: On February 6, 2026, DHS issued a press release naming specific individuals with criminal records — including child sex offenders, domestic abusers, and an alleged gang member — and accusing "agitators and sanctuary politicians" of shielding them from arrest. The release named two Minnesota cases and three from other states. DHS warned that "obstructing law enforcement is a felony and a federal crime." The release was accompanied by Fox News coverage including a viral video of an ICE agent in St. Paul telling community members they were disrupting the arrest of a child sex offender.

incidents.title: Trump Says Administration Will Use "Softer Touch" After Minneapolis Shootings
incidents.summary: In an NBC News interview ahead of the 2026 Super Bowl, President Trump said the federal government could use "a little bit of a softer touch" in Minneapolis following the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens by federal immigration agents. Trump called the people his agents killed "not angels," saying: "He was not an angel, and she was not an angel." He blamed Governor Tim Walz and Mayor Jacob Frey for lack of cooperation, repeated claims about targeting "criminals" that fact-checkers found inaccurate, and framed the draw down as a concession rather than a response to public backlash.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Racial Profiling Allegations Are "Disgusting, Reckless and Categorically FALSE"
incidents.summary: On January 30, 2026, DHS Assistant Secretary for Public Affairs Tricia McLaughlin issued a statement categorically denying that ICE engages in racial profiling. The statement came as multiple U.S. citizens reported being stopped, detained, and in some cases injured by federal agents based on their appearance rather than any immigration violation.

incidents.title: Noem Defends "Domestic Terrorist" Claim: "Best Information We Had at the Time"
incidents.summary: On January 29, 2026, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem defended her characterization of Alex Pretti as a "domestic terrorist" by stating officials were using "the best information we had at the time." She described the scene as "chaotic" but did not retract the claim. This statement came after her own agency's internal report to Congress made no mention of Pretti attacking officers or brandishing a gun—directly contradicting her initial public statements.

incidents.title: Homan Takes Command, Begins Operation Metro Surge Draw Down
incidents.summary: Following two fatal shootings of U.S. citizens by federal agents, the Trump administration restructured Operation Metro Surge. Border czar Tom Homan was sent to Minneapolis to take direct command, Gregory Bovino was removed, and a phased reduction of federal officers began. The draw down was framed as a response to "unprecedented cooperation" from local officials, though local officials immediately disputed this characterization.
incidents.latestUpdate: Governor Walz [says he expects drawdown](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-news/walz-says-he-anticipates-significant-reduction-in-ice-surge-in-minnesota-as-early-as-next-week/) in "days, not weeks and months" after conversations with Homan (Feb 9) and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles (Feb 10). City of Minneapolis estimates $100 million in cumulative economic losses.

incidents.title: DHS Response: ICE Officers Face "8,000% Increase in Death Threats"; Publishes Minnesota Voicemail
incidents.summary: On January 26, 2026, DHS issued a press release claiming an 8,000% increase in death threats against ICE officers and their families. The release included the transcript of a threatening voicemail left for a Minnesota-based ICE officer on January 24, 2026. DHS blamed "sanctuary politicians" — naming Governor Tim Walz and Mayor Jacob Frey — for inciting the threats through their "repeated vilification and demonization of law enforcement." DHS has not provided underlying data supporting the 8,000% figure; this statistic was first used in an October 2025 press release.

incidents.title: Bovino Tells CNN Agents Are "The Victims" in Pretti Shooting; Says Second Amendment Rights "Don't Count"
incidents.summary: In a CNN "State of the Union" interview with Dana Bash the morning after Alex Pretti was fatally shot by federal agents, Border Patrol Commander Gregory Bovino claimed his agents were "the victims." When Bash pointed out that Bovino had repeatedly referred to Pretti as a "suspect" while defending the agents' actions, she said, "With respect, it feels as though in some ways you're blaming the victim here." Bovino replied: "The victim? The victims are the Border Patrol agents. I'm not blaming the Border Patrol agents. The suspect put himself in that situation." When Bash asked if exercising Second Amendment rights could result in being shot by federal law enforcement, Bovino stated: "We respect that Second Amendment right. But those rights don't count when you riot and assault, delay, obstruct and impede law enforcement officers."

incidents.title: Bovino on Pretti: "Let's Take a Look at the Gun"; Second Amendment Groups Raise Concerns
incidents.summary: At a press conference following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti, Border Patrol Commander Greg Bovino was asked whether Pretti ever reached for or brandished his weapon. Bovino stated the matter was under investigation: "This is under investigation. Those facts will come to light, but let's take a look at the gun." Rather than directly answering whether Pretti reached for his weapon, Bovino pivoted to displaying a photo of Pretti's firearm, describing it as "semi-automatic high capacity type, possibly a SIG Sauer." The shooting has sparked concern from Second Amendment advocacy groups, who argue that merely possessing a legal firearm does not justify lethal force. Gun Owners of America, Second Amendment Foundation, and Minnesota Gun Owners Caucus have all called for a full investigation.

incidents.title: Bovino Blames Politicians, Community Leaders, and Journalists for "Tragic Consequences"
incidents.summary: At a press conference the day after Alex Pretti was fatally shot by federal agents, Border Patrol Commander Gregory Bovino blamed politicians, community leaders, and journalists for what he called "tragic consequences." Bovino stated that those who "vilify law enforcement" by calling agents "Gestapo" bear responsibility for "consequences" and "what we saw yesterday" — an apparent reference to the Pretti shooting — though he never explicitly articulated how criticism of law enforcement caused the shooting. When asked directly if DHS would take responsibility for the fatal shootings, Bovino declined to answer.

incidents.title: Vance on Pretti: "Engineered Chaos" Unique to Minneapolis
incidents.summary: Following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti, Vice President JD Vance posted on X claiming "this level of engineered chaos is unique to Minneapolis" and is "the direct consequence of far left agitators, working with local authorities." Vance provided no evidence to support his assertion that Minneapolis resistance was organized differently than other cities or that local authorities coordinated with protesters.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Pretti "Violently Resisted"
incidents.summary: Following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti by federal agents, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, White House advisor Stephen Miller, and other administration officials have consistently claimed Pretti approached officers with a handgun and "violently resisted" attempts to disarm him. Video from multiple angles shows Pretti was holding a phone, not a weapon, and that his gun was removed from its holster by an agent before he was shot. At a press conference, Border Patrol Commander Greg Bovino defended the shooting, claiming the officer fired "defensive shots" and that federal law enforcement had been "under attack" in Minneapolis. Bovino described the officer as "highly trained" with eight years of experience. Video shows multiple agents had Pretti on the ground when he was shot.
incidents.latestUpdate: [U.S. District Judge Eric Tostrud denied](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-02/minnesota-loses-bid-to-force-noem-to-preserve-shooting-evidence) the State of Minnesota's request to extend a temporary order requiring DHS Secretary Noem to preserve all evidence related to the fatal shooting.

incidents.title: Vice President Vance Defends 5-Year-Old's Detention: "What Are They Supposed to Do?"
incidents.summary: Vice President JD Vance visited Minneapolis on January 23, 2026, and addressed the detention of 5-year-old Liam Conejo Ramos. Vance defended ICE's actions, arguing the alternative would have been to "let a 5-year-old child freeze to death" and that exempting parents from arrest would grant universal immunity. Critics disputed his key claims, including the "freeze to death" scenario and his characterization of the family's legal status.

incidents.title: Bovino: "We Are Experts in Dealing With Children"
incidents.summary: At a press conference in Minneapolis on January 23, 2026, Border Patrol Commander Greg Bovino defended ICE's detention of children, declaring "We are experts in dealing with children. Not because we want to be, but because we have to be." The remarks came amid national outrage over the detention of a 5-year-old and a 2-year-old in Minneapolis earlier that week. ICE official Marcos Charles also accused the 5-year-old's father of "abandoning his child" during the arrest.

incidents.title: DHS Response: "Child Was ABANDONED," Father "Fled on Foot"
incidents.summary: DHS posted on X responding to reports that ICE agents used a 5-year-old child as "bait" during a January 20 arrest in Columbia Heights. DHS claims ICE "did NOT target a child" and that the father "fled on foot—abandoning his child" when agents approached. School officials provided a different account of the sequence of events.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Agents "Harassed" at Gas Stations, Used "Crowd Control Measures"
incidents.summary: DHS posted on X claiming Border Patrol agents were "repeatedly harassed and blocked by hostile crowds" while taking bathroom breaks at gas stations in Minneapolis-St. Paul. DHS states someone spit on an agent, the crowd "tackled and attacked the agents," and agents "had to use crowd control measures to disperse the hostile crowd."

incidents.title: Trump on ICE Violence: "Mistakes Happen" While Focusing on "Murders and Criminals"
incidents.summary: At a White House briefing marking one year in office, President Trump acknowledged ICE agents "make mistakes sometimes" while defending enforcement operations. Trump displayed arrest records at the podium, stating agents are "apprehending murderers and drug dealers." Civil rights organizations and critics have characterized enforcement incidents as systemic rather than isolated.

incidents.title: Trump Claims ICE Operation is About Removing "Murderers & Criminals" from Minnesota, Calls Protesters "Highly Paid Troublemakers"
incidents.summary: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social claiming ICE is capturing "murderers & criminals" and that there are "thousands of vicious animals in MN alone." He praised ICE agents as "Patriots" and dismissed protesters as "highly paid troublemakers."

incidents.title: DHS Response: Defends Detention of Hmong Citizen, Claims Sex Offender Targets at Large — Family Disputes Claims
incidents.summary: A DHS response posted on X defends the detention of a U.S. citizen (ChongLy Scott Thao) at his St. Paul home, claiming ICE was conducting a "targeted operation" for two convicted sex offenders who "remain at large." The statement claims the citizen "refused to be fingerprinted or facially ID'd" and "matched the description of the targets."

incidents.title: DHS Secretary Noem Defends Raids as Targeting 'Criminals and Rapists,' Denies Pepper Spray Use on CBS
incidents.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem denied on CBS's "Face the Nation" that federal agents had used pepper spray and similar tactics curtailed by a judicial order, claiming the judge "told us we couldn't do what we already aren't doing." When CBS showed video evidence, Noem shifted her position, stating agents "only use those chemical agents when there's violence happening."

incidents.title: DHS Response: Kneeing Victim is "Criminal Alien from Ecuador"
incidents.summary: When asked about video showing a Border Patrol agent kneeing a man in the face at least five times while other agents pinned him to the ground, DHS told CNN the victim is a "criminal alien from Ecuador." A GoFundMe claims he is a legal U.S. resident. Neither claim has been independently verified.

incidents.title: DHS Statement: Defends Accent-Based Detention
incidents.summary: DHS posted on X defending the detention of a U.S. citizen whose accent was used as basis for suspicion. DHS claims the individual "at first lied about where he was born, claiming Minnesota" and later "changed his answer to Mexico." Records revealed he was a naturalized U.S. citizen and he was released. The statement explicitly confirms the agent "recognized one individual's accent as being from Mexico" as grounds for initial suspicion.

incidents.title: Trump Threatens Military Deployment to Minneapolis Under Insurrection Act
incidents.summary: President Trump threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act to deploy military forces to Minneapolis, warning he would use the law if "corrupt politicians" don't "obey the law and stop the professional agitators and insurrectionists." The Pentagon subsequently placed 1,500 active-duty troops from the 11th Airborne Division in Alaska on standby for possible deployment. Trump walked back the threat a day later, and troops were stood down after the second fatal shooting of a U.S. citizen by federal agents.
incidents.latestUpdate: [Northern Command orders troops to stand down](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/us/politics/alaska-north-carolina-troops-minnesota-deployment.html). The second fatal shooting of a U.S. citizen (Alex Pretti on Jan 24) "galvanized public sentiment against the federal government's tactics and forced the administration to retreat."

incidents.title: DHS Blames Mayor Frey's Sanctuary Policies for Criminal Release
incidents.summary: DHS issued a statement criticizing Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey's sanctuary city policies, claiming they have resulted in the release of "nearly 470 criminal illegal aliens" back onto Minnesota streets since President Trump took office. The statement centered on a vehicular homicide case as evidence for why sanctuary policies are "dangerous."

incidents.title: Border Patrol Commander Bovino CBS Interview
incidents.summary: U.S. Border Patrol Commander Gregory Bovino sat down with WCCO's Esme Murphy for an interview defending ICE operations in Minnesota. During the interview, Bovino claimed "90% to 95% of Minnesotans" support the immigration crackdown and stated U.S. citizens have "no reason to be scared." CBS News noted they could not find any polling to support the 90-95% claim. Bovino's assurance to citizens is contradicted by documented cases of U.S. citizens detained, injured, and hospitalized during Minnesota operations.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Native American Detentions
incidents.summary: After four Oglala Sioux Tribe members (U.S. citizens) were detained near Little Earth, DHS refused to provide information unless the tribe entered into an ICE cooperation agreement. The tribe declined, citing treaty violations. ICE and DHS did not respond to media requests for comment.

incidents.title: DHS Demands Minnesota Honor 1,360+ ICE Detainers
incidents.summary: DHS issued a statement demanding Governor Tim Walz and Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey honor ICE arrest detainers for "more than 1,360 criminal illegal aliens" in state custody. DHS claimed Walz has "released nearly 470 criminal illegal aliens back onto the streets" since President Trump took office. The Walz administration disputed these numbers, stating only 207 people are on ICE detainers in the Minnesota prison system.

incidents.title: DOJ Declines Civil Rights Investigation into Good Shooting
incidents.summary: Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche announced there is "no basis for a criminal civil rights investigation" into the shooting death of Renee Good by ICE agent Jonathan Ross. Six federal prosecutors in Minnesota resigned, citing concerns about DOJ pressure to investigate Good's activist ties rather than the shooting itself.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Speedway Bystander "Hit an Officer"
incidents.summary: DHS posted on X stating that a U.S. citizen bystander at the Speedway gas station arrest "did not comply with the lawfully given order, and instead responded by hitting an officer." Multiple video angles from the scene show a different sequence of events, with the citizen appearing to comply before being tackled.

incidents.title: DHS Response: "Radical Rhetoric" From "Sanctuary Politicians" Causes 1,300% Increase in Assaults
incidents.summary: On January 8, 2026, DHS issued a press release claiming a 1,300% increase in assaults on ICE officers and a 3,200% increase in vehicular attacks, blaming "sanctuary politicians" and their "radical rhetoric" for inciting violence against law enforcement. The release specifically cited Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey's statements. DHS has refused to provide underlying data for these claims; independent analysis by NPR and CPR News found the actual increase in federal court filings for assault on federal officers was approximately 25%.

incidents.title: DHS Statement: "Worst of the Worst" Arrests Jan 8
incidents.summary: DHS issued a press release highlighting 13 individuals arrested in Minneapolis, claiming all had serious criminal histories including sexual assault, drug trafficking, and violent crimes. This was part of their daily "worst of the worst" communications strategy.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Good "Weaponized Her Vehicle"
incidents.summary: Hours after ICE agent Jonathan Ross shot and killed Renee Good, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem and spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin stated Good "weaponized her vehicle" in an attempt to run over officers, calling it "an act of domestic terrorism." Multiple independent video analyses have presented different interpretations of the events.
incidents.latestUpdate: [New York Times reports](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/07/us/renee-good-investigation-minnesota-trump.html) FBI Director Kash Patel and senior officials ordered agents to stop a civil rights investigation into the shooting before a signed search warrant could be executed on Good's vehicle. Officials were concerned the evidence — blood spatter and bullet trajectories — would contradict Trump's claim that Good "violently, willfully, and viciously ran over the ICE Officer." DOJ leadership instead pushed prosecutors to investigate Good herself and her widow, Becca Good, for ties to protest groups. At least 14 prosecutors have since resigned from the Minnesota U.S. Attorney's Office.

incidents.title: DHS Response: Abdulkadir Abdi "Gang Member"
incidents.summary: In the first Operation Metro Surge press release, DHS labeled Abdulkadir Sharif Abdi as a current gang member. This characterization differs from a 2018 federal court finding that he had "turned his life around" and his family's statements that he is not currently in a gang.
